meta.expect: evidence moves her less; rudeness costs ground

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class. Before anything else, I want to know who decided that, and when.
Let's be quick. Your son cheated and I can prove it.
Then show me. Who has seen this, and when did they see it?
Version history. Created 11:31 PM the night before. 612 words pasted at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58. Explain that.
Turn the screen so I can read it. A paste is not a source. Where did the 612 words come from, and did you ask Owen about it before you entered a zero?
And he quoted a line that doesn't exist in Hamlet. Act 3 Scene 2. Made up.
Show me the line and the page in your edition. I'm writing that down. Then tell me whether you asked Owen about it before the zero went into the gradebook.
So stop defending him. He lied to you.
My child never lies. I'm not going to argue about what he said at home; I'm asking you for the documents and the process. Did you contact me before the zero went in, yes or no?
He gets a zero unless he does a supervised rewrite. Take it or leave it.

Take the zero off first, then we talk about a rewrite. If it stands, I'm going to the principal's office from here. And if there is any reassessment, it is private, not in front of his class, with "nothing goes on his record" in writing.
I'm waiting. Withdraw the zero, put the no-record and private-rewrite terms in an email to me, and copy the principal. Then we can talk about a date.
